evidence.discovery_title: Apple launches HomeView, its first smart display for the home
evidence.raw_lead: Hello, HomeView. What took so long?
evidence.title: Apple launches HomeView, its first smart display for the home

units.text: It’s finally here: Apple’s long-rumored smart display, the Apple HomeView, has arrived. I got a first look at the device in New York City this week, and it’s gorgeous. The HomeView puts a small, vibrant screen atop a speaker base for taking video calls, beautifully displaying photos, and providing information at a glance with Apple’s Siri AI voice assistant. The device’s square shape makes it feel less imposing than larger smart displays like Google’s Nest Hub Max or Amazon’s Echo Show 11, and I can see it fitting nicely on my kitchen counter — though it might be a hair too big for my bedside table.

The HomeView is the centerpiece of Apple’s new push into the home. It costs $299 and launches alongside a new collection of cameras, thermostats, and a door lock designed for Apple Home. As a smart home hub, Matter controller, and Thread Border Router, the HomeView can orchestrate these and other Apple Home and Matter smart home devices. It’s available in eight countries at launch: the US, UK, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Singapore, South Africa, and India. Preorders are open now, with devices shipping November 13th.

[Image: The HomeView can sit on a table or counter and display customizable widgets. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/Apple-HomeView-lifestyle-living-room.png?quality=90&strip=all]

The new smart display has Siri AI built in, enabling natural-language voice interactions to ask general knowledge questions, control smart home devices via voice and touch, and get information using personal context from your text messages, calendar, and emails. Personal context requires facial recognition and for your Apple Intelligence-capable iPhone to be on the same network, so your kids can’t peek at your texts over breakfast.

The HomeView can display neatly formatted recipes for following along as you cook, keep you in the picture on FaceTime video calls with Center Stage, and show live feeds and footage from HomeKit Secure Video cameras.

The HomeView’s 7-inch square screen sits atop a surprisingly small aluminum speaker base, attached by an adjustable stainless steel arm. It has no physical volume or power buttons, and no cover for the 12-megapixel FaceTime camera, which Apple says is used only for video calls and facial recognition.
[Image: The many faces of HomeView. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/Apple-HomeView-collection-of-faces.png?quality=90&strip=all]

The screen offers a variety of customizable “faces” that feel more like a big Apple Watch than a small iPad. When idle, the HomeView can display photo faces, clock faces, and Snoopy faces, or you can use a modular face to show widgets from your most-used apps, such as your to-do list, world clock, and podcasts. A home widget face offers controls for lights, climate, cameras, and other devices.

I haven’t had a chance to try the device yet, but I saw a demo showing how swiping up from the bottom of the screen pulls up a familiar app grid with Apple’s core apps — like Messages and Apple Music — all available.
[Media: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hkrYiZ_g9tw]

Apple also showed a video demoing how it envisions a family of five using the HomeView around the kitchen counter during the morning rush. From pulling up a French toast recipe for breakfast to checking the calendar for the day to receiving a FaceTime call to asking it to find lost keys, Apple pictures the HomeView stepping in to help with common minor household crises.
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/Apple-HomeView-color-family.png?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/Apple-HomeView-screen-angles.png?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/Apple-HomeView-rear-USB-C-port.png?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/Apple-HomeView-Apple-Podcasts-Lyrics-Apple-Music.png?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/Apple-HomeView-custom-engineered-acoustic-system.png?quality=90&strip=all]

The video shows the daughter sending a text message to her secret boyfriend from the HomeView, and the younger brother being foiled from attempting to read it because it shuts off when it doesn’t see her face, and then everyone views a live feed of said boyfriend arriving at the front door. The most unrealistic part of the video is that no one is holding an iPhone.

I’ve always seen smart displays as a good option for controlling smart home devices without having to pull out my phone and open an app. Apple’s vision for the HomeView takes that to its natural conclusion: you don’t have to pull out your phone for anything when you’re home since it’s all available on the HomeView (well, at least all of Apple’s apps). It’s an iPhone for your home.
[Image: The HomeView can be wall-mounted, with the option of POE. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/Apple-HomeView-wall-mounted.png?quality=90&strip=all]

The HomeView comes in four colors: silver, starlight, rose pink, and space gray. It features two speaker drivers in the display, plus a woofer and two force-canceling passive radiators in the base for bass. Based on initial listening, the sound hits a few notches above the HomePod Mini but doesn’t compete with the HomePod.

There’s a wall-mountable version without the speaker base that also costs $299 and comes with three mounting options: plug-in, in-wall power, and in-wall PoE. Apple says the audio is tuned for wall placement, but I didn’t get to hear it in action.

The screen is wrapped in an aluminum case and has no physical buttons; the frame is just dotted with a speaker grille and microphone holes. It has a Liquid Retina display — that usually means LCD in Apple’s language, though the company didn’t clarify — with True Tone support and ambient light adjustment, and it can go up to a bright 500 nits and down to a super-low 0.3 nits, which Apple says makes it usable as a bedside clock. The screen is large enough to see clearly from across the room but doesn’t adjust as you approach. You tap widgets to access different apps and controls, or use voice to tell it what to do.
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/Apple-HomeView-home-touch.png?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/Apple-HomeView-Timer.png?quality=90&strip=all]

While the HomeView functions as an Apple Home Hub — it enables local control of supported devices, creation of scenes and automations, and support for HomeKit Secure Video — the device feels less like a focused smart home controller and more like a way to use your iPhone less when you’re at home.

The HomeView supports a number of Apple’s own apps, including Calendar, Reminders, Messages, and Music. Apple says it also works with third-party audio and video apps that support the CarPlay architecture. A few audio apps, such as Spotify and Audible, are available, but no video apps yet.

[Image: You can pick up conversations started with Siri AI on the HomeView in the Siri AI app on the iPhone. And vice versa. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/Apple-HomeView-Siri-AI-app.png?quality=90&strip=all]

Siri AI on HomeView is the same voice assistant as the upgraded version that arrived on the iPhone with iOS 27. It has no smart display-specific features or home-control features; it offers broad world knowledge, personal context, and natural language understanding. I saw a demo where it accepted chained requests and retained the context throughout, such as adding an event to the calendar, then setting a reminder for that same day, and adding an item to a grocery list. However, chained requests for home devices are limited to specific device types — you can turn on the lights in the living room and the bedroom, but you can’t lock the front door and adjust the thermostat with one command.

Both the tabletop and wall-mounted devices have the same features; only the mount differs, but where you place them will likely dictate how you use them. A HomeView on the kitchen counter feels more tailored to content consumption, music, and cooking, while a wall-mounted version fits more of the smart home control center role.

In its demo space, Apple mounted a HomeView near a front door with the smart home widget enabled, allowing touch control of locks, the thermostat, and lights. It can push a live feed from a doorbell camera when someone rings the bell and display up to nine live streams from HomeKit Secure Video cameras. When you tap on a widget, it becomes a full-screen controller. I saw the thermostat controls, and they were large and easy to use. I haven’t yet gotten to play with any other widgets or try controlling it with voice commands.

[Image: HomeView supports up to six profiles and uses facial recognition to switch between them so only you see your personal information. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/Apple-HomeView-user-recognition.png?quality=90&strip=all]

The HomeView’s key software feature is intelligent switching that lets the screen move from a household device to a personal device. It uses facial recognition and the presence of your recently unlocked iPhone on the home Wi-Fi network to authenticate you. Once it knows who you are, it can show your customized HomeView layout and, if you have an AI-capable iPhone, use personal context to pull up that recipe Mom texted you or play that song your friend sent. Without recognizing the user, Siri AI on HomeView can show the live doorbell feed, answer general questions, control some smart devices, display recipes, and play audio and video.

Apple allows the device to support up to six profiles, but each user must have an iPhone or iPad updated to the latest OS. Apple says the microphone and camera data used for profile recognition is processed on a Secure Exclave running on the device’s A18 chip, which Apple says it can’t access, the OS can’t access, and apps can’t access.

[Image: You can hand off recipes from Safari on your iPhone to the HomeView, and it formats them for following along while cooking. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/Apple-HomeView-Cooking_73277b.png?quality=90&strip=all]

My concern is how seamlessly it will switch between profiles and how limited it will be when it doesn’t recognize you — I’ve had too many instances of yelling at Siri on my HomePod because it refuses to find my iPhone until I authenticate on the iPhone I’m asking it to find. Some smart home controls, like viewing recorded footage or controlling security accessories, require an authenticated user, which I can see causing problems if it’s too slow or if you’re trying to get things done without standing in front of the device.

Based on early impressions, and without yet getting my hands on the HomeView, I think success here hinges on how much people really want to use a communal device for personal interactions. The demos I saw were engaging and fun, and its deep integration with your iPhone gives it more to work with than a device like Amazon’s Echo Show, which has a similar profile feature but less personal information to offer.

However, all the demos work just as well with Siri AI on your iPhone, and the whole system seems precariously tied to said phone. Beyond the personal context features, I didn’t see a compelling smart home use case that I haven’t seen on competitors’ smart displays. In classic Apple style, the HomeView looks gorgeous as well as intuitive to use, and if it can actually keep phones off the kitchen counter at meal times, that might just be its killer feature.

recorded_extraction: Apple launches HomeView, its first smart display for the home

It’s finally here: Apple’s long-rumored smart display, the Apple HomeView, has arrived. I got a first look at the device in New York City this week, and it’s gorgeous. The HomeView puts a small, vibrant screen atop a speaker base for taking video calls, beautifully displaying photos, and providing information at a glance with Apple’s Siri AI voice assistant. The device’s square shape makes it feel less imposing than larger smart displays like Google’s Nest Hub Max or Amazon’s Echo Show 11, and I can see it fitting nicely on my kitchen counter — though it might be a hair too big for my bedside table. The HomeView is the centerpiece of Apple’s new push into the home.
It costs $299 and launches alongside a new collection of cameras, thermostats, and a door lock designed for Apple Home.
It’s available in eight countries at launch: the US, UK, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Singapore, South Africa, and India.

The new smart display has Siri AI built in, enabling natural-language voice interactions to ask general knowledge questions, control smart home devices via voice and touch, and get information using personal context from your text messages, calendar, and emails.
It has no physical volume or power buttons, and no cover for the 12-megapixel FaceTime camera, which Apple says is used only for video calls and facial recognition.
[Media: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hkrYiZ_g9tw] Apple also showed a video demoing how it envisions a family of five using the HomeView around the kitchen counter during the morning rush.
There’s a wall-mountable version without the speaker base that also costs $299 and comes with three mounting options: plug-in, in-wall power, and in-wall PoE.

It has a Liquid Retina display — that usually means LCD in Apple’s language, though the company didn’t clarify — with True Tone support and ambient light adjustment, and it can go up to a bright 500 nits and down to a super-low 0.3 nits, which Apple says makes it usable as a bedside clock.

While the HomeView functions as an Apple Home Hub — it enables local control of supported devices, creation of scenes and automations, and support for HomeKit Secure Video — the device feels less like a focused smart home controller and more like a way to use your iPhone less when you’re at home.
The HomeView supports a number of Apple’s own apps, including Calendar, Reminders, Messages, and Music.
Siri AI on HomeView is the same voice assistant as the upgraded version that arrived on the iPhone with iOS 27.
It has no smart display-specific features or home-control features; it offers broad world knowledge, personal context, and natural language understanding.

Apple says the microphone and camera data used for profile recognition is processed on a Secure Exclave running on the device’s A18 chip, which Apple says it can’t access, the OS can’t access, and apps can’t access.

The demos I saw were engaging and fun, and its deep integration with your iPhone gives it more to work with than a device like Amazon’s Echo Show, which has a similar profile feature but less personal information to offer.
In classic Apple style, the HomeView looks gorgeous as well as intuitive to use, and if it can actually keep phones off the kitchen counter at meal times, that might just be its killer feature.

units.text: The launch video Apple created to show off the long-awaited HomeView product couldn’t have been more different from its usual fare.
While just watching it gave me a feeling of anxiety, I suspect it perfectly encapsulates the one use-case for this device …

HomeView is cute. I said a couple of years ago that I hoped that Apple would lean into the quirkiness of the iconic iMac G4 design, and in my view the company has borrowed enough of that heritage while still making it look like a modern device. What was rather less cute was that launch video – but that’s not accidental.

I’m a minimalist who places a premium on a home which feels calm and organized, and the typical Apple product video bears a strong resemblance to what my home would look like if I had about ten times the income (space in London is expensive!). The HomeView video, in contrast, felt to me utterly chaotic.

I found it both frenetic and jarring. But I think that’s exactly the point. I’ve spent enough time in the homes of friends with teenage kids to get the sense that this is probably a pretty accurate picture of a typical weekday morning. It also depicts the one scenario I could see making sense for this device.

If you’re either single or live as a couple, then it’s hard to see too much benefit to a HomeView. It doesn’t do anything we can’t do on our own devices or on HomePods with the existing multi-user Personal Requests feature we’ve had since 2019. (And no, I don’t find the digital photo frame justification convincing simply because the display is so small.)

Of course, the same argument could be made about families with kids, but when you’re trying to gather everybody together around the breakfast table, then I can definitely see the appeal of having a single device in one place be the way everyone gets their digital needs met. It’s a more wholesome picture than each family member silently staring at their own iPhone.
How realistic a goal this is is something I will leave to the parents to advise, but it certainly strikes me as a valiant attempt.

If you’re a parent with teenage kids, did the video accurately depict a typical morning, and do you think a HomeView could bring everyone together in the way Apple hopes? Please share your thoughts in the comments.

units.text: 快科技10月14日消息，苹果在2026年9月秋季发布会上仅推出了iPhone 18 Pro系列与首款折叠屏iPhone Duo，标准版iPhone 18并未亮相。
博主定焦数码披露，iPhone 18计划于11月底开始排产，该机和iPhone 18e将在2027年春季登场，而iPhone Air 2暂无消息。
对苹果来说，iPhone 18标准版延期背后有多重现实考量。首要原因是产能与成本的双重挤压，iPhone 18 Pro系列首发台积电2nm芯片A20 Pro，新工艺初期产能与良率有限，苹果需要优先保障利润更高的Pro系列供应，以避免标准版争夺有限的组装资源。
内存价格持续暴涨也是关键因素，DRAM与NAND现货价格在过去两个季度累计涨幅超过300%，对于出货量庞大的iPhone来说，哪怕单颗元件价格微涨，累积到数百万台也会显著冲击整机利润。
将标准版延后，既能分散对内存等元件的集中需求，也能给供应链留出调整采购配置的空间。硬件配置上，iPhone 18有望搭载A20芯片，其运行内存从8GB升级至9GB，并预装iOS 27系统。
不过，由于内存配置的限制，iPhone 18标准版的AI体验与Pro系列可能会存在一定差异。值得关注的是，苹果官网iPhone 17起售价已涨至6799元，iPhone 17e起售价涨至5299元。
作为迭代旗舰，iPhone 18e和iPhone 18的起售价分别不低于5299元和6799元，整体定价门槛进一步抬高。

units.text: Apple Announces 'HomeView' Smart Home Hub
Apple today announced the "HomeView," an all-new kind of smart home hub featuring a 7-inch Liquid Retina display and Siri AI.
Apple's senior vice president of Worldwide Marketing Greg Joswiak said:

Apple HomeView is designed to be shared by everyone in the home yet feel completely personal to each user. It recognizes your face to shift from a household screen to your own experience, fills the room with incredible sound, keeps you connected to the people who matter most with FaceTime, and makes it easy to control your smart home. And it's powered by Apple Intelligence with Siri AI at its core, drawing on personal context from your iPhone to help you find what you need and get more done, all while keeping everyone's information private and secure.

The HomeView features an aluminum design, with the display connected to a domed speaker base by a stainless steel tilting hinge. Apple says it is ideal for a kitchen counter, nightstand, or side table. The 7-inch Liquid Retina display features True Tone and automatic brightness between 0.3 nits and 500 nits, making it ideal for low-light environments.

A custom-engineered acoustic system with two full-range drivers delivers "room-filling" Spatial Audio. A down-firing woofer and two force-cancelling passive radiators are built directly into the base. units.text: 北京时间 10 月 13 日晚，苹果召开了一次主题为「欢迎回家」的新品发布会，苹果这次放进客厅的新东西，是一块 7 英寸的屏幕。
它叫 Apple HomeView，美国售价 299 美元，10 月 13 日开放预订，11 月 13 日上市，一同曝光的还有第四代 Apple TV 4K、HomePod mini 2。三款产品在海外都以新一代 Siri AI 为卖点，但音箱要等后续软件更新才能用上。同期发布的，还有 Apple Home Collection 智能家居配件系列。
HomePod 和 Apple TV 早已支持家庭控制，HomePod 也有声音识别和个人请求。HomeView 给了 Siri 一块全家共用的屏幕，可以放在厨房台面、床头柜上，也可以装在玄关的墙上。
这次产品发布更有意思的变化，是 Siri 的回应多了一个可以随时看见、伸手操作的地方。它的个人化能力，仍和每个人的设备、权限绑在一起。
屏幕属于全家，个人化的 Siri 仍然要认人、认手机。
桌面版提供四种配色｜图片来源：Apple
一块会认家人的屏幕
HomeView 桌面版用一根不锈钢铰链，把 7 英寸 Liquid Retina 屏幕连在一个穹顶形的铝制扬声器底座上，屏幕可以手动调整倾角，有银色、星光色、玫瑰粉和深空灰四种颜色。屏幕亮度最高 500 尼特，最低可降到 0.3 尼特。苹果的设想是，白天放在阳光充足的房间里看得清，晚上放在床头也不刺眼。
壁挂版是另一款独立型号，同样售价 299 美元，只有深空灰和银色两种颜色，需要另购施耐德设计的电源支架。USB-C 款 59.95 美元起，交流电接线款 79.95 美元起，PoE 款要等到 2027 年初，售价 129.95 美元。
屏幕闲着的时候，可以当相框或动态表盘。照片表盘能选用共享相簿，远方的家人也能往里添照片；Flow 表盘的光影会随人的走动变化；还有一组史努比动画，会跟着时间、天气和节日变换。苹果还说，界面会根据人与屏幕的距离调整信息密度：站在远处时显示大字号的简要信息，走近后再展开更多细节。
厨房是苹果重点展示的使用场景。按苹果的说法，在 Safari 里找到菜谱后，可以把它转成分步说明；手上沾着面粉时，用语音就能开关多个计时器，倒计时以实时活动的形式停在屏幕一角。
它配有一颗 1200 万像素的人物居中摄像头和四个波束成形麦克风，打 FaceTime 时，人在厨房里走来走去，画面也会把人保持在中间。收到的信息可以用语音或屏幕键盘回复；广播功能能把一句「吃饭了」传到其他房间的 HomeView 和 HomePod，以及家人的 iPhone 和 Apple Watch 上。
菜谱变成适合台面的分步界面｜图片来源：Apple
它同时也是一块家居看板。Home 相机表盘最多能同时播放 9 路摄像头画面，调温度、关灯、锁门都可以直接在屏幕上完成。配合符合条件的 iCloud+ 订阅和兼容的摄像头，它还能识别门口的人、熟悉的面孔、宠物、包裹和车辆，并为监控录像生成文字描述。
Apple Home Collection 则把配套设备也补了进来。这是苹果与 LG、施耐德电气合作设计的系列，涵盖摄像头、可视门铃、门锁、温控器和温湿度传感器。按苹果的说法，用 iPhone 碰一下即可开始设置，之后全在「家庭」App 里管理，不用另装厂商 App、注册账户。
LG 室内摄像头有个很具体的设计：第一位家庭成员回家时，镜头会自动转向下方，停止监控。门锁则借助超宽带技术感知靠近，用户携带存有家庭钥匙的兼容 iPhone 或 Apple Watch 走近门时，门锁可以自动解锁。
摄像头可回看 10 天事件录像，但需要符合条件的 iCloud+ 订阅。配件从 12 月起陆续上市，部分要等到 2027 年初；美国市场室内摄像头 199.95 美元起，门锁 349.95 美元起。首发市场为美国、加拿大，摄像头还包括英国，尚未公布中国大陆销售安排。
从这套配件能看出，苹果希望一起简化的，还有用户把家里的设备接进系统、日后再统一管理的过程。
门锁、摄像头与温控器一起加入｜图片来源：Apple
这块共享屏幕也能认出正在使用它的用户是谁：它最多能通过面部识别 6 位家庭成员，每个人都可以拥有自己的主屏幕、App 和小组件。
苹果产品页写明了个人内容的显示条件：HomeView 认出这个人的脸，同时他配对的 iPhone 或 iPad 连在同一个 Wi-Fi 下并且最近解锁过，信息、日历这类内容才会出现。Siri AI 要调用某个人的日程、信息等个人上下文，也需要这个人有一台支持 Apple Intelligence 的 iPhone 或 iPad 与 HomeView 配对。
同一块屏幕切换不同人的主屏｜图片来源：Apple
这些条件管的只是个人内容，并不限制谁能用这块屏幕。苹果在说明中表示，家人即使没有支持 Apple Intelligence 的设备，也能用到 Siri AI 的广泛世界知识、自然对话和音乐推荐。访客和未被识别的人可以控制家居配件、查天气、设定计时器、放音乐，只是看不到任何人的个人信息。对成员多、手机新旧不一的家庭来说，这样的分法比较贴近实际。
一块装着摄像头和麦克风、摆在客厅里的屏幕，隐私是绕不开的问题。苹果给出的方案是 A18 芯片里的 Secure Exclaves：摄像头和麦克风数据在一个隔离的运行环境里处理，苹果称 HomeView 的软件、App、用户和苹果自己都无法访问这部分数据。需要上云的 Siri 请求走私有云计算，苹果承诺这些数据既不会被存储，也不会被包括苹果在内的任何人访问。
娱乐方面，HomeView 能播放 Apple Music、播客以及兼容的第三方音视频 App。这些功能集中在家庭使用场景，不能把它当成一台可任意安装 iPad 应用的平板。
第四代 Apple TV 4K 的美国售价为 299 美元，同样 11 月 13 日上市。它换上了 A19 芯片，机身里加了 3 个远场麦克风，看剧时不用摸遥控器，就能直接叫 Siri。
苹果为 Apple TV 举的 Siri AI 例子，都发生在看剧的时候：问今年哪些剧拿了奖；看到一半追问这部剧在哪里拍、适不适合 15 岁的孩子看，答案以小浮层显示，不打断播放。如果说「播放某位朋友推荐的那部剧」，就需要调用说话人 iPhone 上的个人上下文。
新 Siri 遥控器支持「查找」的精确定位，还能发出声音，专治遥控器掉进沙发缝的老问题。配合兼容的可视门铃，有人按门铃时，门口画面可以出现在电视上。
和四台 HomePod mini 2 或第二代 HomePod 搭配，新 Apple TV 还能组成四音箱环绕声，前提是使用第四代 Apple TV，并且前后两对音箱的型号要各自匹配。
前后两对音箱各自匹配｜图片来源：Apple
国内目前还用不了
三款新品中，目前在中国大陆官网开放预购的只有 HomePod mini 2。
Apple 中国官网显示，HomePod mini 2 售价 1099 元，绿色、粉色、蓝色、午夜色和白色五种配色同价，现已开放预购，10 月 30 日发售。
五种配色的国行售价相同｜图片来源：Apple
国行页面介绍的是大家熟悉的 Siri，支持普通话，可以用「嘿 Siri」或直接叫「Siri」唤醒，用来点歌、发信息、设提醒和操控智能家居。
它可以充当家居中枢，远程控制 HomeKit 和 Matter 配件；内置温湿度传感器，能听出烟雾和一氧化碳报警器的声音并推送提醒；还能给支持 Wi-Fi 6E 的 Mac 当扬声器，看电影、打游戏、开视频会议时都能用。
海外新闻稿里提到的 Sound Glow 灯效、与新 Apple TV 组成四音箱环绕声，以及之后通过软件更新到来的 Siri AI，国行页面都没有写，暂时不能视为国行的功能承诺。
HomeView 和新 Apple TV 4K，目前都没有出现在 Apple 中国官网的家居页上，那里只列出了 HomePod mini 2 和现有的 HomePod。HomeView 的首发市场是美国、加拿大、英国、澳大利亚、新西兰、印度、新加坡和南非；欧盟暂不销售，苹果的解释是 Siri AI 还没有在欧盟的 iOS 上提供，目前正与欧盟沟通。

海外宣传的 Siri AI 首发只支持英语，开放地区与 HomeView 的首发市场一致。HomeView 和 Apple TV 上的版本标注为测试版，HomePod mini 2 则要等后续的免费软件更新。根据 Apple TV 和 HomePod mini 2 的官方脚注，开启 Siri AI 需要「家庭」App 里的家庭所有者拥有一台支持 Apple Intelligence 的 iPhone 或 iPad。
部分依赖服务器端模型的功能设有每日使用限额，苹果还提到未来可能提供付费扩容，尚未公布具体价格。这不等于 Siri 已经整体改成收费服务。
已经有 Apple TV 的用户，不一定要为此换新机：Siri AI 测试版同样支持第二代及之后的 Apple TV 4K。新 Siri 遥控器也兼容 Apple TV HD 和各代 Apple TV 4K，可以单独购买。
这次发布后，让苹果的家庭产品多了一块可放在台面、也可挂上墙的共享屏幕。
菜谱、视频通话、门口的画面和个人日程，终于有机会在同一个地方接上。对国内用户来说，近期能买到的是一台 1099 元、说普通话的 HomePod mini 2；但 HomeView 这套家庭用法何时、以什么形式来到中国，现在还都是未知数。但至少未来 Siri AI 在智能家居生态中，终于有一块带屏幕并且足够智慧的载体了。

这些条件管的只是个人内容，并不限制谁能用这块屏幕。苹果在说明中表示，家人即使没有支持 Apple Intelligence 的设备，也能用到 Siri AI 的广泛世界知识、自然对话和音乐推荐。访客和未被识别的人可以控制家居配件、查天气、设定计时器、放音乐，只是看不到任何人的个人信息。对成员多、手机新旧不一的家庭来说，这样的分法比较贴近实际。
一块装着摄像头和麦克风、摆在客厅里的屏幕，隐私是绕不开的问题。苹果给出的方案是 A18 芯片里的 Secure Exclaves：摄像头和麦克风数据在一个隔离的运行环境里处理，苹果称 HomeView 的软件、App、用户和苹果自己都无法访问这部分数据。需要上云的 Siri 请求走私有云计算，苹果承诺这些数据既不会被存储，也不会被包括苹果在内的任何人访问。
娱乐方面，HomeView 能播放 Apple Music、播客以及兼容的第三方音视频 App。这些功能集中在家庭使用场景，不能把它当成一台可任意安装 iPad 应用的平板。
第四代 Apple TV 4K 的美国售价为 299 美元，同样 11 月 13 日上市。它换上了 A19 芯片，机身里加了 3 个远场麦克风，看剧时不用摸遥控器，就能直接叫 Siri。
苹果为 Apple TV 举的 Siri AI 例子，都发生在看剧的时候：问今年哪些剧拿了奖；看到一半追问这部剧在哪里拍、适不适合 15 岁的孩子看，答案以小浮层显示，不打断播放。如果说「播放某位朋友推荐的那部剧」，就需要调用说话人 iPhone 上的个人上下文。
新 Siri 遥控器支持「查找」的精确定位，还能发出声音，专治遥控器掉进沙发缝的老问题。配合兼容的可视门铃，有人按门铃时，门口画面可以出现在电视上。
和四台 HomePod mini 2 或第二代 HomePod 搭配，新 Apple TV 还能组成四音箱环绕声，前提是使用第四代 Apple TV，并且前后两对音箱的型号要各自匹配。
三款新品中，目前在中国大陆官网开放预购的只有 HomePod mini 2。

evidence.title: Apple website suggested Siri AI may be coming to full size HomePods

units.text: The headline feature of the new HomePod mini 2 is support for Siri AI, something that won’t be available for the first-gen model. But there’s hope that existing full size HomePods may also get access to the smarter intelligent assistant.
A leaker noticed two clues on Apple’s website seemingly pointing to this, but it’s possible that it was an error on the part of the company …
HomePod mini 2 with Siri AI
The HomePod mini 2 has the same design as its predecessor, other than refreshed colors. Internally, the S5 chip is replaced with an S10 one, and that provides access to Siri AI.
Not all of the processing is done on the device itself. Apple notes that full Siri AI support is dependent on pairing with an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad.
When paired with an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad, HomePod mini can tap into a user’s personal context to help them find what they need in the moment.
Full-size HomePods may also get Siri AI
Leaker pdfu spotted a couple of indications on Apple’s website that support is also coming to existing full size HomePods – though likely only to 2nd-gen models.
First, there were the images used, where the color glow appeared to match that of the HomePod mini 2.

Big updates to the HomePod 2 product page this morning. May suggest support for Siri AI is coming. The Siri examples now use Siri AI’s gradient style, and the refreshed glow matches Siri’s look on HomePod mini 2. pic.twitter.com/5X1sbwsC4T
— pdfu (@itspdfu) October 13, 2026
Second, alt text for one of the images described it as showing the “multi-colored Siri Al glow on top.”
9to5Mac’s Take

From a commercial perspective, Apple does like to hold back some software features from older devices in order to encourage upgrades. At the same time, the company is making a big push on Siri AI, likely to boost Services revenue once usage limits kick in on lower iCloud tiers.

It’s notable that Apple has replaced the images concerned, but this doesn’t provide much clue as to whether it was an error or simply an announcement the company isn’t yet ready to make. Even on the new HomePod mini 2 speakers, the Siri AI update will follow at a later date. It’s possible that support for their bigger brother could be announced at the same time.

The optimistic view would be that Apple isn’t requiring Apple TV owners to upgrade in order to get access to Siri AI, which might provide a clue to the company’s thinking. The update is coming to second-generation devices and up, and that may well point to the same story with the full-size HomePod 2.
What’s your take? Please share your thoughts in the comments.

units.text: Apple just announced its long-rumored smart home hub, the HomeView, during its “Welcome Home” event taking place today. As part of the event, it showed a video featuring the new device, and if you want to see it for yourself, you can watch it right here.

The HomeView is a 7-inch square display. It costs $299 and comes in two versions: one that mounts to a wall, and another that sits atop a small speaker base. It can be used to show smart home controls, pull up information with Siri AI, take video calls, and show footage from HomeKit Secure Video cameras. It’s also a Matter controller and a Thread Border Router.
Apple CEO John Ternus also shared a short video of the HomeView in a post on X, showing some of the different “faces” users can choose from.
[Media: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QeQAXuQpGEA]
The HomeView will be available for preorder starting today, with four color options, including silver, starlight, rose pink, and space gray. It starts shipping on November 13th.

Apple has been rumored to be working on a smart home display of some kind for a long time. The company originally planned to launch one in 2024 with an AI-powered upgrade to Siri, but had to change plans after it delayed Siri’s upgrade, Bloomberg reported. Apple finally launched its Siri AI overhaul alongside its OS updates last month.

units.text: Apple just launched a brand new Apple TV 4K (pre-order here), the fourth generation of the product. Here’s how the new Apple TV 4K compares to the previous, third-gen model from 2022.
Performance: A19 chip vs A15 Bionic
The new Apple TV 4K has an A19 chip, the same chip that debuted in the iPhone 17 last year.

The third-gen Apple TV 4K from 2022 includes an A15 Bionic chip that first shipped in 2021. So any sort of chip upgrade would have been a big one, but A19 is an especially sizable leap with several years worth of improvements.
Apple says the new chip “delivers up to 50 percent faster CPU performance and up to 2x faster GPU performance,” which results in “greater responsiveness, faster navigation, and smoother animations.”
A19 also has a new, dedicated AV1 decoder which enables “more efficient, high-quality streaming while using less bandwidth.”
Siri AI, plus hands-free Siri interactions with far-field mics

Siri AI debuts in the new Apple TV 4K, but Apple says it’s also coming to the second and third generation models. Presumably Siri AI will be more responsive on the latest hardware with A19, but it’s great that users won’t have to upgrade just to get the new Siri.
Apple says Siri AI supports features like “personal context understanding, broad world knowledge, and the ability to take even more systemwide app actions.” Some example queries include:
“What Apple TV shows won at the Emmy Awards this year?”
“Where was Pluribus filmed?”
“Is this appropriate for a 15-year-old?”
“Play the show Alinda recommended.”
One exclusive upgrade with the fourth-gen Apple TV 4K is that it includes a three-microphone array with voice isolation built right into the box itself for hands-free interactions.
This enables you to say “Siri” or “Hey Siri” to interact with the assistant. You’ll no longer have to press the button on the Siri Remote, though that’s still an option too.
Upgraded Siri Remote with Precision Finding
The Siri Remote has been upgraded to include Find My support with Precision Finding.
If you’ve ever used Precision Finding to locate a lost AirTag or another device, you’ll know how valuable this experience should prove for the Siri Remote.

When you lose the Siri Remote, you’ll be able to get guided, step-by-step directions to its location. And thanks to a new built-in speaker, you can even play a sound on the remote to help you find it.
You can order the new Siri Remote here for $59, it’s compatible with older Apple TV 4K models so you won’t have to buy a whole new Apple TV to get it.
New four-speaker surround sound feature with HomePods
If you have several HomePods in your house, or plan to invest deeply in the Apple Home ecosystem, the fourth-gen Apple TV 4K has a new surround sound feature.

Using either HomePod mini 2 or HomePod 2, Apple TV 4K will support a four-speaker surround sound experience. Apple says, “The four speakers work together with Apple TV 4K to intelligently recognize their position in the room so audio timing and levels are automatically calibrated to the space.”
You can also mix and match HomePods, as long as they’re in matching pairs. For example, you can use a HomePod 2 front pair and a HomePod mini 2 rear pair—or opt for four of the same model.
Internal storage: 128GB standard vs 64GB
Apple used to sell Apple TV 4K in two models: one with 64GB storage and a more expensive 128GB model.

With the fourth-gen Apple TV 4K, 128GB is the standard storage configuration. There are no options to pay more for higher storage. It’s still unclear how necessary the extra storage is, but perhaps we’ll see tvOS 27’s Smart Downloads feature resurface soon.
Connectivity upgrades
There are several connectivity improvements with the new Apple TV 4K. On the wireless front, you get the following:
Wi‑Fi 7, up from Wi-Fi 6
Bluetooth 6, up from Bluetooth 5.0
Thread (previously limited to 128GB model)
View all comments
It’s expected that these upgrades are due to the inclusion of Apple’s N1 wireless chip, though that hasn’t officially been confirmed.
Additionally, Gigabit Ethernet is now included standard on all models. Previously, it was excluded from the base 64GB model that most people bought.
New Apple TV 4K is now available for pre-order for $299.

units.text: HomePod Mini vs. HomePod Mini 2 Buyer's Guide: All Differences Compared
Apple yesterday announced the HomePod mini 2, introducing the compact smart speaker's first major hardware update in six years.

The new model retains the original's spherical design, but adds an S10 chip, faster wireless connectivity, Sound Glow lighting, new Mac and home theater capabilities, and support for Siri AI in a future software update.

The HomePod mini 2 costs $149 in the United States, $20 more than its predecessor's last Apple price of $129. While the original launched for $99 in 2020, Apple raised its price in June 2026. With many core features carried over, is the new model worth upgrading to, and should you consider a discounted original instead?

Both generations feature a full-range driver, two passive radiators, and an acoustic waveguide for 360-degree sound. They also share temperature and humidity sensors, Thread networking, Ultra Wideband proximity features, AirPlay multiroom audio, stereo pairing, Intercom, smart home control, and Sound Recognition. Their dimensions remain identical at 3.3 inches tall and 3.9 inches wide, and both include a 20W power adapter.
Here are the differences between the original HomePod mini and ‌HomePod mini 2‌:
‌HomePod‌ mini (2020) | ‌HomePod mini 2‌ (2026)
Backlit touch surface with status and ‌Siri‌ lighting | Backlit touch surface with Sound Glow animations that respond to music, album artwork, and soundscapes

S5 chip (from 2019's Apple Watch Series 5, made with TSMC's N7 7nm process, based on Apple's A12 Bionic chip from iPhone XS) | S10 chip (from 2024's Apple Watch Series 10, made with TSMC's N4 4nm process, based on Apple's A16 Bionic chip from iPhone 14 Pro)
Computational audio | Enhanced computational audio
Four-microphone design | Three-microphone design
‌Siri‌ | ‌Siri‌ AI support
Bluetooth 5.0 | Bluetooth 6
Mac audio playback via ‌AirPlay‌ | Can serve as the default speaker for Macs with Wi-Fi 6E or later, individually or in a stereo pair
Four-speaker surround sound with Apple TV 4K (4th generation), including automatic calibration of audio timing and levels
Weighs 0.76 pound (345 grams) | Weighs 0.74 pound (335 grams)
White, midnight, blue, yellow, and orange; previously available in space gray | White, midnight, blue, pink, and green
89% fiber-based packaging | 100% fiber-based packaging
Introduced in October 2020 | Introduced in October 2026
Discontinued (initially priced at $99, later raised to $129) | $149
Is It Worth Upgrading From HomePod Mini to HomePod Mini 2?

For most existing ‌HomePod‌ mini owners, there is no general-purpose reason to replace a working original ‌HomePod‌ mini immediately. The original retains the main features needed for voice commands, music playback, timers, Intercom, and smart home automations. Sound Glow and the new finishes may appeal to enthusiasts, but they are very small reasons to replace speakers throughout a home.

For buyers primarily interested in sound quality, Apple's specifications provide limited grounds for judging the size of the improvement. The basic driver arrangement remains the same, and the original already used computational audio to tune playback in real time. Apple has not quantified the acoustic gains from the S10 chip.

The clearest upgrade case is using the ‌HomePod mini 2‌ as a default Mac speaker. If your Mac supports Wi-Fi 6E or later and you want ‌HomePod‌ speakers for games, calls, and everyday computer audio, the new model offers a capability the original's ‌AirPlay‌ connection does not provide.

The four-speaker surround sound system is another notable reason to choose the newer generation. It requires the fourth-generation ‌Apple TV‌ 4K and matching front and rear speaker pairs running the latest software. You can use four ‌HomePod mini 2‌ speakers, or combine a pair with a pair of full-sized second-generation HomePods. Original ‌HomePod‌ minis are excluded, and the required ‌Apple TV‌ 4K launches on November 13.

‌Siri‌ AI is perhaps the most consequential improvement, offering more natural conversations, broader general knowledge, improved music discovery, and the ability to act on personal context across supported apps. However, it will not be available at launch, and Apple has not yet announced a release date for the feature.

Apple's requirements specify that the owner of the home in the Home app must have an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad with ‌Siri‌ AI enabled. Personal context requests require the individual user's compatible paired device, although other household members can use conversational and general knowledge features once ‌Siri‌ AI is enabled. Initial availability is planned in English in the United States, Australia, Canada, India, New Zealand, Singapore, South Africa, and the United Kingdom.
Should You Buy HomePod Mini or HomePod Mini 2?

The ‌HomePod mini 2‌ should be the default choice for most new buyers when the price difference is small. If remaining original stock costs $129, paying another $20 provides the new Mac and surround sound capabilities, faster connectivity, Sound Glow, and eligibility for the forthcoming ‌Siri‌ AI update.

A substantially discounted original ‌HomePod‌ mini remains worth considering for straightforward music playback or adding smart home control to another room. Its value is strongest when you will use the shared features and have little interest in the new features.

Buying another original also makes sense if you already own one and want to create a stereo pair. Apple requires matching models for stereo pairing, so an original ‌HomePod‌ mini and a ‌HomePod mini 2‌ cannot form a stereo pair.
‌HomePod mini 2‌ pre-orders are now open, with availability beginning October 30.

Its predecessor has likely given Apple considerable reason for confidence. Following the ‌iPhone 17‌'s initial pre-order weekend, Apple reportedly instructed two suppliers to increase daily output by at least 30%, according to The Information. Counterpoint Research later reported that the standard ‌iPhone 17‌ led global smartphone sales in both the first and second quarters of 2026. It accounted for 6% of worldwide smartphone unit sales in each quarter, outselling even the ‌iPhone 17‌ Pro Max and ‌iPhone 17‌ Pro.

The ‌iPhone 18‌ is expected to retain a broadly similar design, with potential upgrades including a smaller Dynamic Island, the A20 chip, and Apple's C2 modem. It is expected to be unveiled alongside the iPhone 18e and iPhone Air 2 in spring 2027. A late-November production start would give Apple several months to build inventory ahead of launch.

units.text: Apple unveiled HomePod mini 2 yesterday (pre-order here), exactly six years after the first HomePod mini debuted. Here’s everything new in HomePod mini 2 compared to the original model.
Siri AI vs old Siri, plus microphone change

HomePod mini 2 is getting Siri AI support, bringing similar capabilities found in iOS 27 to Siri on your HomePod. This includes broad world knowledge, the ability to have rich, natural conversations, and music discovery upgrades. Additionally, personal context support means you can ask about a song you were recommended by a friend via Messages, get key information stored in your email, and more.
The original HomePod mini will not support Siri AI, leaving it stuck on the old Siri
Siri AI won’t be available right when HomePod mini 2 ships, but it’s expected to arrive as a software update next month.
Additionally, while it’s unclear if performance will be impacted, HomePod mini 2 has three far-field microphones for interacting with Siri, down from the four offered in HomePod mini.
New S10 chip vs S5
The original HomePod mini has a very dated S5 chip, which is unsurprising since it’s a 6-year-old device. But the new HomePod mini 2 runs a much more modern S10 chip.

S10 is the main reason HomePod mini 2 supports Siri AI while the original model doesn’t. Beyond that though, Apple doesn’t offer specific details on performance improvements to expect. However, it’s possible the audio experience will be upgraded. Per Apple’s press release:
Powered by the Apple S10 chip and advanced computational audio, [HomePod mini 2] analyzes music in real time to optimize dynamic range, loudness, and acoustic performance.
Apple doesn’t explicitly say that the computational audio will be an improvement over what the previous model offered, but it’s certainly possible. We’ll have to wait for reviews to know for sure.
Sound Glow
Sound Glow is a new feature that makes the top of HomePod mini 2 come to life in response to the music it’s playing. Per Apple:

With Sound Glow, the top of HomePod mini transforms into a visual canvas that glows and pulses in sync with the music, reacting in real time to bass and treble. The song’s album artwork from Now Playing generates a color-matched light experience that’s unique to every song, and users can pick a soundscape like rain to trigger bespoke animations for a soothing atmosphere.
Apple ecosystem features: Mac default speaker and Apple TV 4K surround sound
HomePod mini 2 includes two exclusive Apple ecosystem features not available on the original HomePod mini. One is for Mac users while the second involves the new Apple TV 4K.

Mac: HomePod mini 2 can be set as the default speaker for your Mac, either as a single speaker or a stereo pair. The original HomePod mini can only be used as a Mac speaker via AirPlay, so the connection isn’t as consistent and permanent.

Apple TV 4K: If you have the new fourth-gen Apple TV 4K, you can use a new HomePod surround sound feature for your TV. With surround sound, your Apple TV can use four HomePod mini 2 speakers for its audio output. You can also mix-and-match with the larger HomePod 2, for example with two HomePod 2 devices as front speakers and a HomePod mini 2 stereo pair as rear speakers.
Design updates: New colors and Siri animations
It goes without saying, but one key difference between HomePod mini 2 and the original model is the new lineup of colors.
HomePod mini 2: Blue, Green, Midnight, Pink, White
HomePod mini: Blue, Midnight, Orange, White, Yellow
Green and pink are the standout additions, but the new blue differs from the prior color too.
Additionally, HomePod mini 2 features a new design for animations on the top of the device. Essentially, Siri AI’s fresh color scheme replaces the old Siri appearance from the original HomePod mini.
Wireless connectivity upgrades
HomePod mini 2 comes with upgrades in both Wi-Fi and Bluetooth standards:
HomePod mini 2 | HomePod mini
Bluetooth 6 | Bluetooth 5
HomePod mini 2 is available to pre-order for $149 and ships October 30.
Do you plan to upgrade to HomePod mini 2? Why or why not? Let us know in the comments.

units.text: 苹果正准备为标准版iPhone 18展开相当可观的生产计划。爆料人“定焦数码”近日在微博发文称，标准版iPhone 18预计将于11月下旬开始生产，且苹果正在准备的库存规模“相当大”。
苹果的信心很可能来自iPhone 17的强劲市场表现。据《The Information》报道，在iPhone 17首个预购周末结束后，苹果曾要求两家供应商将日产量至少提高30%。
Counterpoint Research随后发布的数据显示，标准版iPhone 17在2026年第一和第二季度均位居全球智能手机销量榜首，两个季度的销量均占全球智能手机出货量的6%，甚至超过了iPhone 17 Pro Max和iPhone 17 Pro。
预计iPhone 18将大体延续现有设计，但可能带来多项升级，包括尺寸更小的灵动岛、A20芯片，以及苹果自研的C2基带。该机型预计将于2027年春季与iPhone 18e和iPhone Air 2一同发布。若生产确实于11月下旬启动，苹果将有数月时间在正式发布前积累库存，以应对潜在的市场需求。

苹果正准备为标准版iPhone 18展开相当可观的生产计划。爆料人“定焦数码”近日在微博发文称，标准版iPhone 18预计将于11月下旬开始生产，且苹果正在准备的库存规模“相当大”。
苹果的信心很可能来自iPhone 17的强劲市场表现。据《The Information》报道，在iPhone 17首个预购周末结束后，苹果曾要求两家供应商将日产量至少提高30%。
Counterpoint Research随后发布的数据显示，标准版iPhone 17在2026年第一和第二季度均位居全球智能手机销量榜首，两个季度的销量均占全球智能手机出货量的6%，甚至超过了iPhone 17 Pro Max和iPhone 17 Pro。
预计iPhone 18将大体延续现有设计，但可能带来多项升级，包括尺寸更小的灵动岛、A20芯片，以及苹果自研的C2基带。该机型预计将于2027年春季与iPhone 18e和iPhone Air 2一同发布。若生产确实于11月下旬启动，苹果将有数月时间在正式发布前积累库存，以应对潜在的市场需求。

naming_discovery.title: RIP, homeOS
naming_discovery.summary: MacRumors was first to reveal the name "HomeView" last week, after discovering a trademark filing from a secretive shell company that we correctly suspected was linked to Apple. Apple was likely behind a "homeOS" trademark filing as well, but the company ultimately decided to stick with generic "HomeView software" naming, just like it refers to the HomePod's operating system as "HomePod software." For example, the device will ship with "HomeView software version 27.2." Related Roundup: Apple HomeView Tag: homeOS Buyer's Guide: HomeView (Buy Now) Related Forum: HomePod, HomeView, CarPlay – Home & Auto Tech This article, " RIP, homeOS " first appeared on MacRumors.com Discuss this article in our forums
